text.p: The shares of SM Summit were suspended from trade on the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES), dealers said on Wednesday.
The stock fell sharply in early morning trade after news of a raid on the company's offices in Singapore.
By the time they were suspended, SM Summit shares were nearly 38 percent lower at Singapore $0.655, down 39.5 cents on active volume of more than 12 million shares.

Officials of the Business Software Alliance told a news conference earlier that SM Summit's offices had been raided in connection with software piracy charges by Microsoft and two other American-listed companies.
SM Summit officials were unavailable for immediate comment but one company employee told Reuters a statement would be issued later.
